lessons.title: Reporting Theft or Loss of Goods
lessons.body: If your goods are stolen in a Spanish-speaking country, go to the nearest police station (comisarÃ­a) immediately. In most countries, you must file a denuncia (official report) within 24 hours for insurance claims. Say: 'Quiero denunciar un robo' (I want to report a theft). Give details: what was stolen, where, and when. For example: 'Me robaron mi cartera en el mercado a las 3 de la tarde' (They stole my wallet in the market at 3 PM). If you lost something, say 'He perdido mi pasaporte' (I have lost my passport). You will need your passport or ID. Ask for a copy of the denuncia; it's called a 'copia de la denuncia'. Keep it safe. In many African countries, police may ask for a 'refresco' (bribe), but in Spanish-speaking countries, it's illegal. If asked for money, politely say 'No entiendo' or ask for a receipt. For stolen phones, report to your operator. In Spain, dial 091 for police; in Mexico, 911. Learn numbers: 1 uno, 2 dos, 3 tres, 4 cuatro, 5 cinco, 6 seis, 7 siete, 8 ocho, 9 nueve, 10 diez. Practice: 'Necesito ayuda, me han robado' (I need help, I've been robbed). Always carry a photocopy of your passport. If you lose goods in transit, contact the transport company. For example: 'PerdÃ­ mi equipaje en el autobÃºs' (I lost my luggage on the bus). They may ask for your ticket number. Use 'Â¿Puede ayudarme?' (Can you help me?). In an emergency, call 112 in Spain, 911 in most Latin American countries. Memorize these phrases: 'Soy extranjero' (I am a foreigner), 'No hablo bien espaÃ±ol' (I don't speak Spanish well). Write down the officer's name and badge number. If you don't understand, say 'Â¿Puede repetir mÃ¡s despacio?' (Can you repeat more slowly?). Get a copy of the report for your embassy. This is crucial for replacing documents. In some countries, you can file online, but in-person is safer. Always stay calm and polite.

lessons.title: Asking for Help in a Medical Emergency
lessons.body: In a medical emergency, call for an ambulance immediately. In Spain, dial 112; in Mexico, 911; in Argentina, 107. Say: 'Necesito una ambulancia' (I need an ambulance). Give your location: 'Estoy en la calle...' (I am on ... street). Describe the problem: 'Mi amigo tiene dolor en el pecho' (My friend has chest pain). If someone is unconscious, say 'EstÃ¡ inconsciente' (He/She is unconscious). For bleeding, say 'EstÃ¡ sangrando' (He/She is bleeding). Learn body parts: cabeza (head), pecho (chest), estÃ³mago (stomach), brazo (arm), pierna (leg). If you are sick, say 'Me siento mal' (I feel bad). For fever: 'Tengo fiebre' (I have a fever). For pain: 'Me duele aquÃ­' (It hurts here). Point to the area. At the hospital, say 'Necesito un mÃ©dico' (I need a doctor). If you have insurance, say 'Tengo seguro mÃ©dico' (I have medical insurance). Show your card. If not, ask 'Â¿CuÃ¡nto cuesta la consulta?' (How much does the consultation cost?). In many African countries, you might go to a clinic first. But in Spanish-speaking countries, hospitals (hospitales) handle emergencies. Pharmacies (farmacias) can help for minor issues. Say 'Necesito medicina para...' (I need medicine for...). For diarrhea: 'Tengo diarrea'. For malaria, say 'Tengo paludismo' (in Spain) or 'Tengo malaria' (in Latin America). Always carry a list of allergies in Spanish: 'Soy alÃ©rgico a la penicilina' (I am allergic to penicillin). If you need an interpreter, ask 'Â¿Hay alguien que hable inglÃ©s?' (Is there someone who speaks English?). But try to use Spanish. Practice: 'Llame a una ambulancia, por favor' (Call an ambulance, please). In an emergency, every second counts. Speak clearly and slowly. If you don't know the word, describe it: 'Un dolor como fuego' (A pain like fire). Keep emergency numbers saved in your phone. Also, learn 'Â¿DÃ³nde estÃ¡ el hospital mÃ¡s cercano?' (Where is the nearest hospital?). For minor injuries, you can go to a pharmacy and ask for 'una curita' (a band-aid) or 'agua oxigenada' (hydrogen peroxide). In case of snakebite, say 'Me mordiÃ³ una serpiente' (A snake bit me). Immobilize the area and get help fast.

lessons.title: Dealing with Police or Officials
lessons.body: If stopped by police in a Spanish-speaking country, stay calm and polite. Say 'Buenos dÃ­as, oficial' (Good morning, officer). Show your ID or passport when asked: 'AquÃ­ estÃ¡ mi pasaporte' (Here is my passport). If you don't understand, say 'No entiendo, Â¿puede hablar mÃ¡s despacio?' (I don't understand, can you speak more slowly?). Police may ask what you are doing: 'Â¿QuÃ© estÃ¡ haciendo aquÃ­?' (What are you doing here?). Answer simply: 'Soy turista' (I am a tourist) or 'Estoy trabajando' (I am working). If they ask for money, it's a bribe. In many countries, this is illegal. You can say 'No tengo dinero' (I don't have money) or 'Prefiero pagar la multa en la comisarÃ­a' (I prefer to pay the fine at the police station). If you are arrested, say 'Quiero llamar a mi embajada' (I want to call my embassy). You have the right to a phone call. Learn: 'No he hecho nada malo' (I haven't done anything wrong). If you are in a car, they may ask for your license: 'Su licencia de conducir, por favor' (Your driver's license, please). Give it. If they claim you broke a rule, ask 'Â¿CuÃ¡l es la multa?' (What is the fine?). Fines are often paid at a bank or police station. Never hand over your passport as a bribe. Keep a photocopy. If you are mistreated, note the officer's name and badge number: 'Â¿CuÃ¡l es su nombre y nÃºmero de placa?' (What is your name and badge number?). Report to your embassy. In some countries, police may target foreigners. Avoid confrontations. If you are innocent, say 'Llame a mi abogado' (Call my lawyer). If you don't have one, ask for a public defender: 'Necesito un abogado de oficio'. In Spain, you can ask for 'asistencia jurÃ­dica gratuita' if you have no money. Always be respectful. Use 'usted' (formal you) with officials. Say 'Gracias, oficial' when leaving. If you are asked to pay a fine on the spot, ask for a receipt: 'Â¿Me puede dar un recibo?' (Can you give me a receipt?). If they refuse, it's likely a bribe. Stay calm and don't argue. Your safety is priority. Memorize: 'No hablo espaÃ±ol muy bien' (I don't speak Spanish very well). This may make them more patient.

lessons.title: Resolving Disputes with Customers or Suppliers
lessons.body: In business, disputes happen. In Spanish, say 'Tenemos un problema' (We have a problem). If a customer complains, listen and say 'Lo siento, Â¿cÃ³mo puedo ayudarle?' (I'm sorry, how can I help you?). If they claim a product is defective, ask 'Â¿Puede mostrarme el producto?' (Can you show me the product?). For a refund, say 'Podemos darle un reembolso' (We can give you a refund) or 'Podemos cambiarlo' (We can exchange it). If you can't agree, suggest 'Hablemos con el gerente' (Let's talk to the manager). For supplier disputes, say 'El pedido llegÃ³ tarde' (The order arrived late). If goods are damaged, say 'Los productos estÃ¡n daÃ±ados'. Ask for a discount: 'Â¿Puede darnos un descuento?' (Can you give us a discount?). If they refuse, say 'Necesitamos resolver esto' (We need to resolve this). In many African countries, business is done face-to-face. In Spanish-speaking countries, it's similar. Use polite phrases: 'Por favor' (Please), 'Gracias' (Thank you). If you need to escalate, say 'Voy a hablar con mi abogado' (I will talk to my lawyer). But try to negotiate first. Learn numbers for prices: 100 cien, 200 doscientos, 500 quinientos, 1000 mil. For a contract, say 'Quiero revisar el contrato' (I want to review the contract). If a customer doesn't pay, say 'Necesitamos el pago' (We need the payment). You can offer a payment plan: 'Â¿Puede pagar en dos partes?' (Can you pay in two parts?). If they still refuse, say 'Tendremos que tomar acciones legales' (We will have to take legal action). But always keep a record: 'Tengo los recibos' (I have the receipts). For suppliers, if quality is bad, say 'No podemos aceptar esto' (We cannot accept this). Ask for a replacement: 'EnvÃ­e un reemplazo, por favor' (Send a replacement, please). If they don't respond, call them: 'Le llamo por el pedido' (I'm calling about the order). Use email for written proof. In Spanish, email is 'correo electrÃ³nico'. Write 'Estimado seÃ±or/seÃ±ora' (Dear Sir/Madam). End with 'Atentamente' (Sincerely). If you need mediation, contact a local business association. In Spain, 'CÃ¡mara de Comercio'. In Mexico, 'CANACO'. They can help. Always stay professional. Don't shout. Say 'Entiendo su posiciÃ³n' (I understand your position). This helps resolve disputes faster.

lessons.title: Contacting Your Embassy or Consulate
lessons.body: If you lose your passport or are in trouble, contact your embassy. In Spanish, say 'Necesito contactar mi embajada' (I need to contact my embassy). Find the address and phone number before you travel. In an emergency, call them. Say 'Soy ciudadano de [paÃ­s]' (I am a citizen of [country]). For example: 'Soy ciudadano de Nigeria'. If you need a new passport, say 'He perdido mi pasaporte' (I have lost my passport). They will ask for a police report: 'Necesito la denuncia de la policÃ­a'. Bring a photocopy of your old passport, photos, and ID. The fee for a new passport varies: in Spain, it's about 30 euros; in Mexico, around 1000 pesos. Ask 'Â¿CuÃ¡nto cuesta el nuevo pasaporte?' (How much does the new passport cost?). If you are arrested, say 'Quiero que notifiquen a mi embajada' (I want you to notify my embassy). The embassy can provide a list of lawyers: 'Necesito una lista de abogados' (I need a list of lawyers). They can also help with medical emergencies: 'Necesito ayuda mÃ©dica' (I need medical help). If you are a victim of crime, they can assist: 'He sido vÃ­ctima de un crimen' (I have been a victim of a crime). For lost money, they may help contact family: 'Â¿Pueden contactar a mi familia?' (Can you contact my family?). But embassies do not give money. They can help you transfer funds. Say 'Necesito recibir dinero de mi familia' (I need to receive money from my family). In some countries, you can go to the consulate for notary services: 'Necesito un notario' (I need a notary). For voter registration, ask 'Â¿Puedo votar desde aquÃ­?' (Can I vote from here?). Always keep your embassy's emergency number. In Spain, many embassies are in Madrid. In Mexico, in Mexico City. In Argentina, in Buenos Aires. If you are in a remote area, call first. Say 'Estoy en [ciudad]' (I am in [city]). They may direct you to a consulate. Learn: 'Â¿DÃ³nde estÃ¡ la embajada de [paÃ­s]?' (Where is the embassy of [country]?). If you don't speak Spanish, ask 'Â¿Habla inglÃ©s?' (Do you speak English?). But try Spanish. Practice: 'Necesito ayuda consular' (I need consular help). Keep a copy of your passport and visa in a safe place. Also, register with your embassy when you arrive: 'Quiero registrarme' (I want to register). This helps in emergencies.

lessons.title: Practice: Role-play a Dispute Resolution
lessons.body: Now practice a dispute resolution. Imagine you are a customer who bought a phone that doesn't work. You go to the shop. Say: 'ComprÃ© este telÃ©fono ayer y no funciona' (I bought this phone yesterday and it doesn't work). The seller says: 'Lo siento, no podemos devolver el dinero' (I'm sorry, we can't refund your money). You reply: 'Pero estÃ¡ defectuoso. Quiero un reemplazo o mi dinero' (But it's defective. I want a replacement or my money). Seller: 'Podemos repararlo' (We can repair it). You: 'No, quiero uno nuevo' (No, I want a new one). If they refuse, say: 'Voy a llamar a la policÃ­a' (I will call the police) or 'Voy a poner una queja' (I will file a complaint). In many countries, consumer protection laws are strong. In Spain, you can ask for 'hoja de reclamaciones' (complaint form). Say: 'Quiero la hoja de reclamaciones'. They must provide it. Fill it out and take a copy. For suppliers, role-play: You ordered 100 shirts but received 80. Say: 'PedÃ­ 100 camisas pero recibÃ­ 80' (I ordered 100 shirts but received 80). Supplier: 'Lo siento, hubo un error' (Sorry, there was a mistake). You: 'Necesito las 20 camisas restantes o un reembolso' (I need the remaining 20 shirts or a refund). Supplier: 'Le enviaremos las camisas maÃ±ana' (We'll send the shirts tomorrow). You: 'Gracias, pero si no llegan, cancelarÃ© el pedido' (Thanks, but if they don't arrive, I'll cancel the order). Always stay calm. Use 'por favor' and 'gracias'. If you need to escalate, say: 'Voy a contactar a un abogado' (I will contact a lawyer). For practice, write a script. Use these phrases: 'Â¿Podemos llegar a un acuerdo?' (Can we reach an agreement?), 'Â¿QuÃ© propone?' (What do you propose?). If you are the seller, say: 'Entiendo su frustraciÃ³n' (I understand your frustration). Offer a solution: 'Le darÃ© un descuento del 10%' (I'll give you a 10% discount). If the customer agrees, say: 'Gracias por su comprensiÃ³n' (Thank you for your understanding). Practice with a friend. Record yourself. Listen for pronunciation. In Spanish, 'r' is rolled. Practice 'reembolso' (refund) and 'queja' (complaint). Also learn 'garantÃ­a' (warranty). Ask: 'Â¿Tiene garantÃ­a?' (Does it have a warranty?). If yes, say: 'Quiero usar la garantÃ­a' (I want to use the warranty). If no, say: 'Entonces quiero mi dinero' (Then I want my money). Remember, in many African countries, negotiation is common. In Spanish-speaking countries, it's similar. Be firm but polite. This role-play prepares you for real situations. Practice until you feel confident.
